questions.question: Cervical lymph node levels (I-VII) are defined by:
choices: Proximity to the carotid artery only
questions.detail: The classification of cervical lymph node levels (I-VII) is strictly based on specific anatomic landmarks.

questions.question: Which level of lymph nodes is located between the medial margins of the anterior bellies of the digastric muscles?
questions.detail: Level IA (submental) lymph nodes are located between the medial margins of the anterior bellies of the digastric muscles.

questions.question: Level IB lymph nodes are submandibular nodes extending to the posterior margin of the:
questions.detail: Level IB represents the submandibular node group, extending posteriorly to the margin of the submandibular gland.

questions.question: Level II nodes extend from the skull base to the inferior margin of the:
questions.detail: Level II (upper jugular) nodes are defined by the space between the skull base and the inferior margin of the hyoid bone.

questions.question: Which structure serves as the boundary between Level IIA and IIB nodes?
choices: Posterior margin of the internal jugular vein (IJV)
questions.detail: Level IIA and IIB nodes are differentiated by their relationship to the posterior margin of the internal jugular vein.

questions.question: Level III lymph nodes (middle jugular) extend from the hyoid bone to the:
choices: Inferior aspect of the cricoid cartilage
questions.detail: Level III nodes, or middle jugular nodes, extend from the level of the hyoid bone down to the inferior aspect of the cricoid cartilage.

questions.question: Level IV nodes (inferior jugular) extend from the cricoid cartilage to the:
questions.detail: Level IV nodes represent the inferior jugular chain, extending from the cricoid cartilage level down to the clavicle.

questions.question: Level V nodes are the ________ cervical nodes.
questions.detail: Level V nodes are defined as the posterior cervical group.

questions.question: The boundary between Level VA and VB nodes is the:
questions.detail: The inferior cricoid cartilage is the anatomical landmark used to separate Level VA from Level VB nodes.

questions.question: Level VI nodes are also known as:
questions.detail: Level VI nodes are identified as pretracheal or visceral nodes.

questions.question: Level VII nodes are superior mediastinal nodes extending from the manubrium to the:
questions.detail: Level VII consists of superior mediastinal nodes ranging from the manubrium to the level of the brachiocephalic vein.

questions.question: Cystic lymph nodes in the neck are most commonly seen in which two cancers?
choices: Papillary thyroid cancer and head/neck SCC
questions.detail: The presence of cystic lymph nodes in the neck is most frequently associated with papillary thyroid cancer and head/neck squamous cell carcinoma.

questions.question: The degree of lymph node involvement is significant because a single node reduces SCC survival by:
questions.detail: Prognostically, even a single metastatic lymph node in patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma reduces the survival rate by 50%.

questions.question: Level VI nodes are bounded laterally by the:
questions.detail: Level VI (pretracheal) nodes are defined laterally by the boundaries of the carotid sheaths.

questions.question: Level I nodes are located ________ to the hyoid bone and ________ to the mandible/mylohyoid.
questions.detail: Level I nodes are anatomically positioned superior to the hyoid bone and inferior to the mandible and mylohyoid muscle.
